To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the (δβ)0-thalassaemia deletion removes the entire β-globein gene and 3′ portion (3′-end) of the δ-gloebin gene.
a 10-kilobase (kb) deletion has occurred in the (delta-beta)-globin gene in (delta beta)-thalassemia to remove the entire beta-globin gene as well as the 3'-end of the delta-globin gene.
a 10-kb deletion has occurred to remove the entire (δ+β) globin genes in (δ+β0)-thalassaemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetics of the globin genes.
the study of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of globin genes in normal and pathological conditions.
the molecular genetics of human hemoglobinopathies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deletion of the δβ-globin genes is due to the deletion of a 10 kb segment of DNA from the 5′ end of the δ-gene to the 3' end of the β-gene.
the (δβ)0-thalassemia gene is a result of deletion of the 5' end of the δ-gene, the entire β-gene and 1.8kb of the 3' end of the γ-gene.
the deletion of the β-gene is a deletion of 10kb and the 5′ and 3′ ends of the deletion are located in the 5′- and 3′-flanking regions of the δ-gene.

we have shown the following: 1.
the deletion is in a region of DNA between 2 kb to the 5′ of the δ-gene and 2.5 kb to the  3′ of the β-gene.

the (δβ)0-thalassaemia deletion occurs in a region of the globin genes which contains no functional genes.
